#e4655d: Proposed dark-theme --danger, because [data-theme='dark'] redefines --positive and neither --danger nor --warning. Measured 5.04:1 against --bg-surface #201D1B and 5.48:1 against --bg-page #171513, where the shipped --red-600 #B3261E scores 2.56:1 and 2.79:1 and fails WCAG AA for body text at 4.5:1 — and .tag--danger is dark-theme text in the backoffice. Same hue and saturation as #B3261E (HSL 3 / 71%), lightness lifted from 41% to 63%: the move the dark theme already makes for --positive (36% to 55%) and --accent (52% to 63%).
#de8e16: Proposed dark-theme --warning. Measured 6.37:1 against --bg-surface #201D1B and 6.93:1 against --bg-page #171513. This one is consistency rather than repair: the shipped --amber-500 #C77F14 already clears AA on dark at 5.17:1 / 5.61:1, but it is the only state colour the dark theme leaves at its light value, and at 5.17 an amber tag reads dimmer than a --positive #8FB463 one (7.08:1) in the same 36px row. Same hue and saturation (HSL 36 / 82%), lightness lifted from 43% to 48%, which lands it between --accent (6.07:1) and --positive.
